findings.message: Task 1.4's AC1 was never actually satisfied by production code: DECK_LESSON_IDS in lessonContent.ts (task 1.1a's file) never gained "lesson-01", so resolveLessonContent("lesson-01") still returned the video arm. lesson01Deck.test.ts's own module comment documented this as a deliberate gap ("Making that edit here was tried and reverted") and its equivalence test explicitly asserted `DECK_LESSON_IDS.has(id)` was false at the end, i.e. the test proved the wiring was absent rather than proving AC1. This is exactly the 'test pinned to the wrong thing reads as covered' failure mode the review role warns about — task 1.4's AC1 [red] proof covered card/vocabulary equivalence, not the actual dispatch behavior AC1 describes ("Opening /lesson/1 renders in-house slides and no video element"). Root cause: a coordination gap between 1.1a and 1.4 — no task's `covers` included both lessonContent.ts and the wiring change, and 1.4 correctly avoided editing a file it didn't own rather than silently breaking 1.1a's tests.

LESSON_ASSET_ROOT (and its Python mirror LESSON_ASSET_URL_ROOT) was "/lessons", omitting the app's deploy base path ("/thai-script/", vite.config.ts:11) that every existing asset URL in the codebase (symbols.ts's ~44 videoUrl/audioUrl fields) is hardcoded with. Confirmed live against the dev server before my fix: fetch("/lessons/lesson-01/deck.json") returned 404 while fetch("/thai-script/lessons/lesson-01/deck.json") returned 200 — so even with F1 fixed, DeckSlide would have shown "Couldn't load this lesson" for every real user. This would have silently broken the entire deck feature in the deployed app despite every unit test passing, since unit tests stub fetch and never exercise the real base path.

e2e/lesson-intro.spec.ts (in task 1.1b's covers, subject of its AC8) still asserted a <video> element and a single-click transition to the maaw-maa card — behavior the phase's own README flagged as 'What will bite' and explicitly assigned to 1.1b to own. 1.1b's AC8 was WAIVED with the stated reason that no verify command runs Playwright, so the break was never observed. Once F1 and F2 are fixed (lesson 1 genuinely deck-served), this spec fails for real, exactly as predicted. Rewrote the spec to assert the deck's opening slide instead of a video, and to drive the deck's own Next/Continue/Show-Answer flow to the maaw-maa card; verified all three cases pass against a live dev server, and re-ran the sibling e2e/home.spec.ts to confirm no other regression.
